The whole place looks different, Ana. When was it built?
It was built in the nineteen forties. Almost everything you see has been redone, little by little.
Did you two knock down that wall yourselves?
No, that one was knocked down by a builder. The wiring and the plumbing were replaced too. That part is not a job for an amateur.
And the floor? It looks original.
It is original. It was stripped and sanded down by hand, by me. Three weekends. But it was worth it.

When people walk into this house, they always ask the same question: how much of it was done by you? The honest answer is about half. The house was built in nineteen forty-six, and it had been empty for years when we bought it. The roof was leaking, the wiring was dangerous, and every wall was damp. The electrics and the plumbing were replaced by professionals, because those two things are not worth the risk. But the floors were stripped and sanded down by hand, by me, over three long weekends. The old doors were repaired and painted in the workshop. Two of them were salvaged from a house down the road that was being knocked down. Nothing here was done quickly. But every time I walk through that hallway, I think: that was worth it.

My renovation was supposed to take eight weeks. It took seven months. The first problem was the plumbing. A leak was found behind the kitchen wall on day three, and everything stopped while it was repaired. Then the beams in the ceiling turned out to be damp, so they had to be replaced as well. The kitchen was delivered twice, because the first one was damaged on the way here. My friends kept asking me if it was worth it, and for a long time I said no. But it is finished now, the light comes in every morning, and honestly, I would do it again. I would just tell myself the truth at the start: whatever number you are given, double it.
